Problem statement

A few cameras. Moving water. Real physics.

Coastal floods, storm surge and breaking waves are usually recorded by only a few cameras. We reconstruct the dynamic scene in 3D over time from such sparse video, and require the result to be physically grounded: the water should conserve mass, travel at the right speed and respect its boundaries, so that wave heights, inundation and what happens next can be read from it.

Sparse views

Two or three distant cameras leave much of the surface seen once or not at all.

Hard appearance

Water is transparent, specular and nearly textureless.

Breaking waves

Crests, spray and foam change shape within a few frames.

Unseen flow

Velocity is never observed and must be inferred from the physics.

Main idea

Generative reconstruction of dynamic scenes

Learning and physics together fill in what the cameras miss.

4D scene evaluation and validation platform

OceanScope

Our research workbench for inspecting and scoring 4D reconstructions against the full simulated ground truth, frame by frame.

Load 4D fieldsSigned-distance and velocity fields for every frame of a sequence.
Inspect in 3DWater surfaces, velocity arrows, cross sections and slices, side by side.
Score every frameErrors and coverage against the ground truth over the whole sequence.
